newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand seen targetting 4.57 - chartists.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand seen targetting 4.57 - chartists.

text.p: The rand sank to its worst level in seven weeks on Thursday with technical indicators pointing to a fresh assault on the key 4.57 level in the short-term, analysts said.
The currency weakened to a morning's low bid of 4.5640 against the dollar -- its worst level since August 22 -- shortly after 0800 GMT after finishing at 4.5375/5425 overnight.
Analysts said Thursday's move had trampled a key chart level at 4.5425 which had pushed the rand into a new 4.54 to 4.57 trading range.

"If it closes tonight above 4.5450 it will bring the 4.57 level into view," Boyde Stafne, technical analyst at UAL Merchant Bank, said, adding that sentiment appeared to be pointing in the same direction.

First National Bank technical analyst Darran Grabham said that the currency's break above the 4.5575 level earlier in the morning was also a bearish signal which pointed to the currency weakening steadily to 4.59 -- its all-time low posted on August 19.
"We went to 4.5650 this morning which was a decent enough break and I think it will weaken slowly towards 4.59," Grabham said.
Traders said that the Reserve Bank had been in the market in a bid to support the currency, although economists noted that the central bank had limited resources given the state of its reserves.
Gross gold and foreign exchange reserves were pegged at 10.04 billion rand in September.
Traders said the currency's move on the day had been driven by mainly London-based dollar demand as well as continuing local importer dollar buying.

While there appeared to be no fundamental reason for the latest bout of dollar buying, some traders pointed to long dollar positions going short on Wednesday in order to avoid carry costs and players then buying back their dollars the following day.
At 0930 GMT, the currency was holding steady at the 4.5560/5610 level.
